I need to estimate software development effort for a software increment described in the specification, which is about Spring Cloud Data Flow / Spring Cloud Data YARN integration features (deploying YARN apps into HDFS, ResourceManager REST API negotiation, multiple app instances, async deployer, resolving module dependent JARs to Boot loader, refactoring ModuleLauncher with Boot's JarLauncher API, documentation and tests, external libraries support).

The user stories are U1-U8. I need to:

2. State technical/design decisions and assumptions
3. Give most likely effort per activity (single estimate, work-hours)
4. Sum total

- Testing (unit, integration)

5. A5: U4 - Asynchronous deployer with task queue

- U4 async deployer: 40h

Technical and design decisions:
- Use Spring Framework 6.x / Spring Boot 3.x with Java 17 baseline (as per spec Spring 6.0 requires Java 17+)
- Use Spring Cloud Data / Spring XD (s-c-d) architecture; extend xd-admin to orchestrate YARN deployments
- Manifest-driven deployment descriptor consumed by xd-admin to determine placement and assets
- HDFS client (Apache Hadoop HDFS API) for staging application artifacts
- YARN ResourceManager REST API (ws/v1/cluster/apps) for app submission; group modules into app instances
- Deployment properties convention module.<label>.yarn.app.* to route modules to named app instances with queue/priority/memory/cpu
- Asynchronous deployment via task executor / queue; shell returns immediately with a task id
- Replace custom ModuleLauncher with Spring Boot JarLauncher/JarFile based classloading; add JAR resolution (e.g., via Maven/Aether) to build classpath
- Uniform external library support via a lib/ directory appended to launcher classpath

Assumptions:
- Existing s-c-d codebase and YARN infrastructure available; Hadoop/YARN version compatible
- One developer (myself) performs all work
- Effort excludes elapsed calendar time; no wait times
- Estimates include unit tests for each implementation activity but integration/system tests separate
- No major changes to Spring Framework itself; work happens in s-c-d/s-c-s modules
- Environment (test YARN cluster, HDFS) available
- Requirements are as stated; no additional scope creep
- Estimates in work-hours, 1 developer

A1: "Technical design and architecture" - Analyze requirements U1–U8; design manifest format, YARN deployment flow, async execution model, JarLauncher-based module launching, external library resolution approach. 24h.

A2: "HDFS deployment support (U1)" - Implement automatic staging/deployment of YARN app artifacts into HDFS, manifest parsing, xd-admin orchestration hooks. 60h.

A3: "ResourceManager REST negotiation (U2)" - Implement client for YARN ResourceManager REST APIs; submit/monitor module groups as YARN applications; handle appType=CLOUDDATA and appName=spring-cloud-data-yarn-app. 64h.

A4: "Multiple app instances (U3)" - Implement deployment property parsing (module.<label>.yarn.app.name), per-app instance configuration (queue, priority, memory, cpu), grouping logic. 40h.

A5: "Asynchronous deployer (U4)" - Implement async deployment execution with task queue; shell returns promptly with handle; status tracking. 40h.

A6: "Boot loader JAR resolution spike (U5)" - Experiment/prototype resolving module dependency JARs and adding them to Boot loader classpath; evaluate approaches. 24h.

A7: "Refactor ModuleLauncher to JarLauncher (U6)" - Refactor s-c-s ModuleLauncher contract onto Spring Boot JarLauncher API; remove duplicated functionality; update tests. 40h.

A8: "Docs and tests for JAR resolution (U7)" - Write reference documentation and test cases for resolving/adding JARs to Boot loader; porting guide. 24h.

A9: "External libraries support (U8)" - Implement uniform mechanism to add external libraries to modules; integration with launcher classpath. 32h.

A10: "Integration and system testing" - End-to-end tests on YARN/HDFS test cluster: deployment, multiple instances, async behavior, external libs. 32h.

A11: "Code review, defect fixing, build/CI and packaging" - Reviews, CI config, defect fixes, release packaging. 24h.

technical_and_design_decisions: Baseline on Spring Framework 6.x / Spring Boot 3.x with Java 17, consistent with the stated Spring 6.0 Java 17+ requirement.
Extend the existing s-c-d (xd-admin) orchestration layer to drive YARN deployments using a manifest file that declares module placement and required assets.
Stage YARN application artifacts (jars, configs) into HDFS using the Apache Hadoop HDFS client API before application submission.
Integrate with the YARN ResourceManager REST API to submit, group and monitor module deployments as YARN applications, honoring appType=CLOUDDATA and appName=spring-cloud-data-yarn-app.
Adopt a deployment-properties convention (e.g., module.<label>.yarn.app.name, plus queue, priority, memory, cpu keys) to map modules to named YARN app instances with distinct queues and priorities.
Implement the deployer asynchronously using a task executor and an internal deployment task queue so the shell returns immediately with a task handle for status polling.
Refactor the s-c-s ModuleLauncher contract onto Spring Boot's JarLauncher API to remove duplicated launching/classloading functionality.
Resolve module dependency JARs at launch time (repository-based resolution) and append them plus user-provided external libraries to the Boot loader classpath in a uniform way.
assumptions: A single developer (the estimator) performs all work; estimates are effort in work-hours, not elapsed calendar time, and exclude waiting/blocking periods.
An existing s-c-d/s-c-s codebase, a build system, and access to a test Hadoop/YARN cluster with HDFS and ResourceManager REST endpoints are available.
No changes to the Spring Framework itself are required; all work occurs in the s-c-d and s-c-s modules described by the user stories.
Each implementation activity includes its own developer-level unit tests; dedicated integration/system testing and documentation are estimated as separate activities.
Hadoop/YARN versions are compatible with the HDFS and ResourceManager REST APIs used; no cluster administration work is included.
Requirements are stable as written; rework due to changing requirements is excluded, while normal defect fixing is covered by the review/fix activity.
The JAR-resolution experiment (U5) is a time-boxed technical spike whose outcome feeds U7 and U8.

activities.activity_description: Analyze U1-U8; design the deployment manifest format, xd-admin orchestration flow, HDFS staging approach, ResourceManager REST integration, async execution model, JarLauncher-based module launching, and the external library resolution strategy.
Implement automatic staging/deployment of the YARN application into HDFS, manifest parsing, and xd-admin orchestration hooks so deployments are placed with the correct assets.

Implement the YARN ResourceManager REST API client to submit and monitor module groups as YARN applications, including appType=CLOUDDATA and appName=spring-cloud-data-yarn-app handling and instrumentation for automatic app instance startup.

Implement parsing of deployment properties (e.g., module.*.yarn.app.name), grouping of modules into distinct YARN app instances, and per-instance configuration of queue, priority, memory and cpu reservations.
Make the deployer asynchronous with a deployment task queue in YARN-facing operations so the shell returns quickly with a handle; add task status tracking and basic lifecycle management.
Time-boxed experiment to resolve module-dependent JARs and add them to the Boot loader, evaluating approaches for handling external libraries required by out-of-the-box modules.
Refactor the s-c-s ModuleLauncher contract to build on Spring Boot's JarLauncher API, remove duplicated launching/classloading functionality, and update affected tests.

activities.activity_name: Docs and tests for JAR resolution (U7)
activities.activity_description: Write reference documentation and test cases covering resolution and addition of JARs to the Boot loader, including a guide for porting modules with external dependencies.
Implement the uniform mechanism to supply external libraries to modules and integrate them into the launcher classpath so modules can consume such dependencies consistently.

End-to-end verification on a test YARN/HDFS cluster: manifest-driven deployment, ResourceManager submission, multiple app instances with differing queues/priorities, async deploy behavior, and external library loading.

activities.activity_name: Review, defect fixing, build/CI and packaging
activities.activity_description: Perform code reviews, configure/update CI build for the new modules, fix defects found during testing, and package the software increment for release.
